newsitem.title: FRANCE: China allocates 20 Airbus A320 jets to airlines.
newsitem.headline: China allocates 20 Airbus A320 jets to airlines.

text.p: China has allocated 20 Airbus A320 single-aisle passenger jets to domestic airlines which were ordered earlier this year, an Airbus spokesman said on Thursday.

Seven of the Airbus Industrie planes have been placed with China Southern Airlines, he said. These are in addition to the 10 allocated to China Southern in April when order contracts were signed by the China Aviation Supplies Corp during an official visit to France by Chinese premier Li Peng.
China Northwest Airlines will get 10 and the remaining three will go to a third company, whose name was not immediately available.
The total order for 30 A320s was estimated to be worth $1.5 billion, the French foreign ministry said at the time.
Deliveries are due to begin in 1997 and continue to the year 2000. No information on the engines was immediately available.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
